questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a new educational culture, but first of all to get an adventure far away from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Regarding visa and needed documents I used a lot of time to find the correct information. The visa process changes over years, wherefore I also sometimes got some wrong/outdated information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance when arriving at the destination.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not attend the orientation events, wherefore it is hard to answer.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was super easy for me, but only because a friend of mine lived in the house in the past semester (also during exchange), and I could therefore takeover her house. San Diego hosts so many Danish exchange each year, so my best recommendation is to use Facebook-groups for Danish exchange students in San Diego.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I am so glad that I lived off campus. I lived at the beach, and really explored and enjoyed San Diego. However, if you are more interested in the american college-life, you should of course live at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hard for me to say, since I did not search for any student-housing at all.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was very easy, and much easier than at KU. The registration process is online, and you can see all steps + there is online assistance.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is online, and you can see all steps + there is online assistance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successfully registered in the classes I wanted. The only problem for me was acceptance from KU, since it took student administration in Copenhagen so long to finally accept my courses that I no longer had the opportunity to change classes at UCSD. Luckily KU accepted the courses, but I would have been in a really bad situation if not.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do as the steps says online, it all makes perfectly sense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are overall at the same level as at KU, however the exams are a lot easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were a lot smaller than at KU, with more conversation during the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Topics of Macroeconomics, Monetary Economics, Economics of Education, Behavioral Economics, Economics of Modern Israel

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Especially Monetary Economics, Economics of Education and Behavioral Economics was super interesting and the courses have really taught me a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxes and tips

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than expected, expect when going to Mexico for spring break:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many sport games, student organisations, etc. were available. When entering campus you are told about all the opportunities, and it is so easy to go there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Check out the student organisations. There is a app showing all possibile. I went with UCSD hiking, it was super cool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car for the whole period, it will make it so much easier to explore San Diego County, California and go to trips in Las Vegas, Grand Canyon, Zion National Park, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was super easy, since the American culture is somewhat close to the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out in Pacific Beach, all students go there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That Americans are so outgoing. It makes it so much easier to socialize with locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have a large savings
2. Live off campus, at either Mission- or Pacific Beach
3. Be open minded

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find Facebook-groups for students in San Diego.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living off campus at the beach, living the beach life with a lot of other international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
